activeCoveredMeaning: active-covered means the current repo has focused adapter/runtime proof and durable operator/source-of-truth evidence for the declared local or Testcontainers profile. It does not mean managed cloud operations, real cluster failover, or L5/L6 chaos proof is complete.

patterns.name: Committed dataset version remains serving truth
patterns.reason: Metadata DB committed dataset versions remain the serving truth even when S3, Iceberg, Spark, or CDC artifacts exist.

patterns.name: Search and CDC projections cannot become source of truth
patterns.reason: Object store and committed dataset state are re-read before sensitive object/search/action decisions.

patterns.name: Dangerous failures leave durable operator evidence
patterns.reason: Adapter, auth, secret, and commit-point failures must be visible in run/error/audit/outbox/trace evidence, not only logs. S56 proves read-only detector reports can surface missing-data, lag, skew, and SLO evidence before source-of-truth rows are mutated, and detect-and-record can persist open/acknowledged/resolved observability_incidents with audit/outbox evidence. S57 proves backup/restore preflight can block DB/storage committed-version mismatches, mark search as rebuildable projection evidence, store only ready preflight evidence as immutable backup artifacts, verify artifact receipts before restore-mode entry, block current-serving-head drift on the validation-only path, execute historical artifact dataset-head restore by copying byte/hash-clean source files into new snapshot versions, keep outbox retry/reprocess closed while restore mode is active, and reject publisher resume until post-restore closed-loop evidence exists. S58A proves local JWT/OIDC bearer-token failures are denied before a Principal is built, M2M service-account tokens remain tenant-scoped, revoked JWT ids are blocked, JWKS refresh/cache behavior is tested, webhook signing secrets are read through SecretProvider and redacted from operator evidence/errors, and REST connector credential secretRefs are re-resolved on the next snapshot after local rotation.

patterns.name: Active stack features retest together
patterns.reason: S3, Iceberg, Spark, and Debezium CDC cannot advance as isolated happy paths once they are active together.

patterns.name: Materialization watermarks are replayable
patterns.reason: Current materialization outputs pin enough cursor state to retry without skipping or duplicating successful rows.

patterns.name: Schema drift is blocked before runtime mismatch
patterns.reason: The schema revision guard protects SQLAlchemy metadata snapshots, fresh Alembic upgrade parity proves a blank DB can reach the current table/column shape, S55 schema migration safety keeps Alembic history single-headed, blocks destructive downgrade schema operations, and now requires phase-tagged expand migrations to declare an old-and-new-app release compatibility window. S55 migration runner proof keeps Alembic execution behind a dedicated singleton DB lock, proves live PostgreSQL advisory-lock contention has one migration callback winner with `lock_busy` evidence for the concurrent runner, and leaves password-masked operator evidence when a migration attempt fails. Dataset schema evolution proof now blocks rename/drop/narrowing-style consumer breaks, records widening/deprecated-field warnings, and creates deterministic backfill progress metadata. Ontology migration proof now blocks property/object/link/action parameter breaking changes before activation, records object reindex plans plus previous/next source-column evidence for property mapping changes, checks generated SDK compatibility, and executes bounded `object_reindex:*` plans through an Operations/API/SDK surface that closes the active object type serving contract as `object_reindex_complete`. The gate also proves additive dataset schema evolution can be followed by ontology mapping migration and reindex against the latest dataset version. Full old/new app deployment windows, object/link remap executors, real backfill execution, and rollback/restore runbook rehearsal remain broader S55 work.

patterns.name: Bad records are quarantined and replayed independently
patterns.reason: S47 now has stream CDC quarantine plus Operations API, typed generated SDK, and Web Operations UI coverage for tenant-scoped dead_letter_records, single and bulk replay idempotency, valid-payload APPEND replay result, replay failure result, discard, audit evidence, DLQ-write fail-closed tests, source-side error threshold fail-closed policy, identity/ordering fail-closed policy, and PostgreSQL concurrent replay request proof. Python transform row-local errors are now quarantined through Input.map_rows(..., on_error="quarantine") with clean-row output commit, transform_execution DLQ metadata, audit evidence, generic replay rejection, and snapshot transform-specific full-rebuild retry. Append/incremental transform DLQ replay remains future until a duplicate-safe merge policy exists.

patterns.name: Late data and watermark movement are explicit
patterns.reason: S48 now has a stream/source archive slice plus snapshot transform output and materialization boundary watermark propagation: StreamArchiveConfig declares event/source time fields, named timezone override, and lateness thresholds, committed archive rows separate event/source/ingest/process time with a late_data_status, too-late records route to Record DLQ, transaction metadata keeps a matching partition/source lateDataWatermark from moving backward without letting unrelated fast-partition watermarks classify slow partitions as stale, duplicate delivery after a committed late event resumes from the durable offset instead of creating a second dataset version, late stream commits expose lateDataSummary, lateDataReprocessingPlan, and a normalized platformWatermark through Operations run detail, snapshot transform output commits derive platformWatermark from input dataset transaction watermarks with a min-input event-time policy while retaining input version/reprocessing evidence, materialization commits expose top-level platformWatermark for action-log and object-snapshot output boundaries plus late-data reopen evidence when a LATE_REQUIRES_REPROCESS CDC index run forces the next closed output to be regenerated, object/materialization explain exposes late-data badges, Operations detail exposes a downstream impact graph for the regenerated materialization, and a late stale CDC delete cannot remove or resurrect the current active object.

patterns.name: Dataset readers use the committed manifest file list
patterns.reason: S49 now has a read/preview, manifest-metadata, local/fake/S3/Iceberg multi-part commit, high-cardinality partition warning, Iceberg file-level pruning, and single-input SQL transform predicate-to-storage proof slice: DatasetStorageAdapter.data_file_paths resolves manifest-listed data files in order, foundry.datasets.preview reads multi-file manifests through the existing facade, unlisted files in the storage directory are not discovered by listing, dataset rows can declare layout policy fields, local/fake/S3 read/preview partition filters reduce actual read files, readable Parquet commit paths record manifest column min/max/null_count and sort_bounds, local/fake storage can commit multiple staged parquet parts into one deterministic manifest/version/DB file-row set, high-cardinality partition layouts persist a warning in committed dataset transaction metadata, validation-after-tamper blocks the commit, stale retry orphan parts are not retained, S3 retries multi-part staged-file commits without duplicate parts, Iceberg commits multiple staged parts into one pinned snapshot with multiple data files, Iceberg skips reads when no manifest file matches, Iceberg column-stat filters download only matching data files without full snapshot materialization, and a single-input SQL transform equality predicate reaches storage partition_filter and compute input file selection. Iceberg maintenance execution is covered by the S50 matrix row.

patterns.name: Iceberg maintenance does not delete serving snapshots
patterns.reason: S50 now has a maintenance planning and bounded execution slice: Operations can request an Iceberg maintenance plan, committed DB dataset-version snapshots are marked protected, compaction candidates are reported from file-count/small-file/read-amplification thresholds, and plan requests leave audit evidence. Operations can also run Iceberg maintenance, compact the current snapshot, verify before/after row hashes match, expire deletable orphan snapshots, delete no-longer-reachable data/sidecar files, keep DB committed manifests readable, and write run audit evidence. Transform/materialization/backup pin retention, concurrent maintenance fencing, fault-injected rollback proof, and ambiguous retry idempotency remain future work.

patterns.name: CDC archive workers can run bounded continuous loops
patterns.reason: S51 has bounded worker loops for stream archive and CDC object indexing plus a resident Source streaming supervisor. Kafka managed Sync partitionMode=all reloads topic metadata, stores independent partition cursors in streamCursors, and a live two-partition broker test proves independent resume without duplicate Dataset event ids. Workflow-run lease owner/token/expiry evidence fences standby workers until expiry and permits takeover afterward; a target Dataset branch single-active guard blocks a second active Streaming Sync. Data Connection exposes partition checkpoints and heartbeat/checkpoint/lag/throughput/failure health rules. The pre-commit assignment guard and CDC object-indexer version cursor remain active. Parallel broker-assigned consumer threads, durable assignment history, real rebalance callbacks, commit-unknown reconciliation, durable incident notification, OS SIGTERM proof, and production daemon packaging remain future work.

patterns.name: Product workflows execute through Temporal
patterns.reason: ConnectorSyncWorkflow now has a product workflow control-plane path through Operations/API/SDK with local/fake/Temporal contract proof, audit-linked ProductWorkflowRun evidence, and a worker-bound Temporal activity proof that commits a local connector snapshot through the normal Dataset ingest boundary. The workflow payload includes a deterministic syncRunId and workflowDefinitionVersion, activity output carries fetch/stage/quality/commit/cursor/event data-plane evidence, cursor advance is proven across workflow starts, and post-commit activity retry reuses the committed sync run without duplicate dataset version or outbox rows. A same-idempotency retry can also reconcile a start_unknown ledger row to the terminal workflow result after the activity already committed the dataset transaction, leaving workflow.reconciled audit/run-relation evidence, and start_unknown retry preserves the originally persisted workflowDefinitionVersion instead of silently switching to a newer code default. Workflow cancel now closes requested/running runs as cancelled with cleanup payload, workflow.cancelled audit, cancelled_by run relation evidence, tenant-scoped adapter cancel behavior, a mismatch guard for adapter-returned run ids, and a terminal-non-cancelled adapter result guard. Continue-as-new, full old-history upgrade replay, managed worker operations, and production connector packaging remain future work.

patterns.name: External writeback uses saga and reconciliation evidence
patterns.reason: S53 now has simulated before-commit writeback slices plus an L8 real S3/MinIO adapter slice, a bounded writeback reconciliation worker slice, a backend approval-release slice and Foundry Operations approval-release UI for sensitive/high-risk recovery, and an AI direct vendor/API egress denial slice. Simulated external-not-changed failures become retryable with external_system_changed=false, retry_after_seconds, same-key replay, queue visibility, and bounded recovery skip evidence instead of automatic reconcile/reissue. Simulated response loss and real adapter timeouts become outcome_unknown, simulated external success and real landed writes followed by local mutation failure become compensation_required, operator-provided remote-success or real adapter remote_lookup catches up the local object mutation while closing action/writeback evidence as reconciled, and the bounded worker can recover non-sensitive unresolved rows using stored externalWritebackUri while leaving audit and JSON evidence. Sensitive/high-risk action-parameter writebacks are skipped as operator_approval_required with approval evidence and no remote lookup/local mutation until the approval-release path receives explicit approval id/reason evidence, records action.writeback.recovery_approved, and reuses the same reconciliation path. Retryable rows are not approval-recoverable. Same-idempotency-key replay does not blindly issue another writeback, concurrent reconcile has one winner, sensitive writeback parameters stay masked in Operations/audit surfaces, and raw HTTP/vendor/webhook/generic executor tool ids are denied by ToolBroker, Agent Runtime, and Visual Builder even when present in a published manifest. ERP-specific connector packaging, connector-backed vendor tool release policy, automatic retry/reissue worker, always-on managed compensation daemon, persistent managed queue UI, reverse/compensation executor, and full managed approval workflow UI remain future work.

patterns.name: Dataset quality uses versioned contract evidence
patterns.reason: S54 slices record the staged candidate fingerprint and schema row/version used by dataset quality check results through checked_manifest_hash, validated_against_schema_version_id, and validated_against_schema_version. When a default DataContract version is active, check results also store data_contract_version_id. Historical check results stay pinned to the schema row/version used by that run after later schema versions are created. Successful check rows are stored as PASS, warning severity failures are visible as non-blocking WARN, and staged candidate tamper or commit-time hard failure is rejected as BLOCK_COMMIT before storage commit. Row-level not_null/unique quarantine checks route failed records to tenant-scoped Record DLQ as DATA_QUALITY_CONTRACT, rewrite the staged candidate to clean records, and revalidate before commit. Operations run detail exposes the transaction-scoped quality summary, schema references, checked manifest hashes, data contract version ids, check results, and up to 5 data-quality quarantine failed-row samples. Persisted quality contract check definitions are create/list/update visible through API/SDK, enabled/config changes are applied by later dataset commit validation when no active contract version overrides them, default DataContract versions can be create/list/get/activate visible through API/SDK, and active versions pin later validation to the checks_snapshot. Accepted-values policy checks now block category/status values outside the active contract snapshot's allowed list. Custom contract-key activation, remaining DataContract policy surface, owner notification, dedicated failed-row sample UI, quality result trend UI, and production DB schema race proof remain future work.
